outcome: Assigning to a name whose class attribute is `None` on a model with `extra='allow'` sets the attribute rather than being treated as an unknown extra

acceptance_criteria.text: Assigning to a name that exists on the class with the value `None` sets that attribute, on a model configured with `extra='allow'`.

expected_verification.assertion: assigning to a class attribute declared as None on an extra='allow' model updates the attribute and does not land in the extras

acceptance_criteria.text: A name that does not exist on the class at all is still collected as an extra, so the fix does not close the `extra='allow'` path.

expected_verification.assertion: assigning an genuinely unknown name on an extra='allow' model still stores it as an extra

data_impact: None. Attribute assignment on an in-memory model instance.
security_impact: None. The change narrows which assignments are treated as unknown extras; it grants no new access.
rollout: Ships with the package. No flag.
rollback: git revert. Before the change, a class attribute whose value was None was indistinguishable from one that did not exist.
